sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that from the perspective of the Torah as given at Sinai there was no forgetfulness, yet speech was still necessary to draw the Torah from concealment into revelation, and the innovation of Yitzchak's blessing is regarding toil in Torah which enables the refinement of Esav.

translations.translation: The explanation is,
that from the aspect of the Torah in its own essence as it was given at the giving of the Torah, there was no matter of forgetfulness at all,
as our sages said,
on the verse,
"engraved upon the tablets,"
and consequently there would have been no need for the matter of toil,
only the matter of speech, etc.
And that speech was necessary in any case is because the giving of the Torah from above at Sinai was given through speech,
therefore it was necessary also in man to have the matter of speech in Torah,
in the manner explained in Torah Ohr,
on the verse,
"And Elokim spoke all these words, saying."
And as the language of our sages,
"Whoever reads and reviews, the Holy One, blessed be He, reads and reviews opposite him."
For seemingly it is not understood why speech is needed in Torah
(whether above or below),
for the matter of Torah is in understanding and comprehension, and it would seem that thought alone should suffice,
so why is the matter of speech necessary, which is an action
(at least a minor one)?
And one cannot answer based on what is said in the Gemara Eruvin
(brought in Tanya),
"If it is arranged in all 248 limbs it is preserved, and if not, etc.,"
for this was only after the second tablets were given,
when the matter of forgetfulness already existed in the world,
but before that, at the giving of the Torah, when there was no matter of forgetfulness, for it was "engraved," etc., as above,
it is not applicable to say so.
Rather, the reason for this is that "Behold, My words are like fire,"
for Torah is compared to fire,
and by way of analogy, when a flame is within the coal it is in a state of concealment,
and to draw the flame into revelation is through a blowing wind,
and similarly in Torah, the matter of speech in Torah was necessary, through which it is drawn from concealment to revelation,
for even from the aspect of the first tablets, the Torah was given specifically below and not above,
as explained in the discourses on the statement of our sages,
"When Moshe ascended on high,"
and therefore the matter of speech in Torah was necessary even without Yitzchak's blessing.
And the innovation in Yitzchak's blessing is regarding the matter of toil in Torah,
through which one can refine even the aspect of Esav,
which is the matter of the sparks in the three impure kelipot
(this was the innovation of the second tablets),
for through this one reaches the aspect of Eden, as above regarding "He does for those who wait for Him," for those who press into matters of wisdom,
and therefore they can refine Esav.
And this is what is said,
"No eye has seen, O Elokim, besides You,"
that they reach the aspect of Elokim that is above revelations,
and therefore it says specifically "And may Elokim give to you,"
that the blessings are drawn from the aspect of Elokim that is above all revelations, etc.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that through "for your seat will be missed," which is total self-nullification even of a point, achieved through toil, one attains "you will be missed," a renewal like the aspect of Eden, leading to Dovid as the eternal leader with the coming of Moshiach.

translations.translation: And this is what is said, "And Yehonasan said to him: Tomorrow is the new moon, and you will be missed, for your seat will be missed,"
that through "for your seat will be missed,"
which is the matter of total self-nullification, even of a point
(which comes through toil),
through this is brought about "you will be missed," which is the matter of renewal in the ultimate sense, like the aspect of Eden, as above,
until "Dovid the great"
etc.,
"and Dovid My servant shall be their prince forever,"
with the coming of Moshiach Tzidkeinu, speedily and truly.
